rationale: Iteration 4 (base_speed 1.1, kp 4.5, kd 0.6, ki 0.3) is the best design so far at 147.1. Lowering speed from 1.4 to 1.1 more than doubled oval progress and tripled s-bend progress. Iteration 5 then changed three controller values at once (base 1.0, kp 5.0, kd 0.7) and fell to 95.1. Oval progress dropped from 0.67 to 0.33 and the oval completion was lost, so the kp increase or the further speed drop hurt. Because the cause is confounded, I revert to the iteration 4 controller and change one variable. Every design still ends at max_error of about 0.060 to 0.064 m, the off-track limit, which points to overshoot on bends rather than slow drift. I raise kd from 0.6 to 0.9 to add damping against that overshoot. Speed (1.1), kp (4.5), ki (0.3) and all geometry stay as in iteration 4 so the kd effect can be read cleanly. Expected result: max_error falls below 0.06 on at least some bends, s-bend progress rises above 0.19, and oval progress holds at or above 0.6 with a chance of more completions. Hypotheses: (H1) if steering_oscillation rises above 0.4 on oval, the derivative is amplifying sensor noise and kd should return to about 0.6 with a different lever. (H2) If max_error is unchanged at about 0.063 on the same bend, the limit is steering authority, and kp or the wheel_track should change next. (H3) If the robot survives all three tracks but does not finish, base_speed should rise to about 1.2 with this kd. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness.
